summary.headline: Satin Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 231% YoY to INR176 crore, but reported returns were held down by a INR14 crore overlay top-up to INR50 crore.
summary.overview: Satin reported a standalone H1 FY27 PAT of INR292 crore, its highest ever, and a consolidated Q2 PAT of INR176 crore, up 231% YoY and 43% QoQ. Slippages fell 68% YoY to INR103 crore in H1, standalone GNPA improved to 1.9% from 2.2% in June, and provision coverage reached 133%. Management added INR14 crore to the management overlay (INR36 crore to INR50 crore), absorbing about 100 bps of ROA that it says would otherwise have been reported. Consolidated AUM grew 31% YoY, but H1 growth of 9% (about 19% annualised) sits just below the 20-25% FY27 guidance range, which management expects to reach.

segments.name: Satin Finserv (SFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,761 crore, up 184% YoY and 29% QoQ across 140 branches in 116 districts-equivalent footprint (as stated); 19 branches added in the quarter. GNPA 3.07% (from 3.49% in June), CRAR 26.94%, net worth INR461 crore; H1 disbursements INR967 crore.

segments.name: Satin Housing Finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,219 crore, up 19% YoY, with CRAR 57.67%, gearing 1.70x, net worth INR370 crore across 59 branches in 22 states. Origination slowed for two quarters while the product is re-engineered toward rural housing; field team raised from 370 to 512.

segments.name: Non-MFI portfolio
segments.commentary: 20% of consolidated AUM versus 15% a year ago; target 30% by 2030.

segments.name: Satin Technologies / QTrino Labs / Satin Growth Alternatives
segments.commentary: Core banking platform in customer UAT; HRMS live in production. QTrino Labs (68% stake) progressing toward certification for quantum-safe cybersecurity. Category II AIF achieved first close in 4.5 months post licence, with first deployment done.

guidance_outlook: Standalone credit cost FY27 guidance of 3-3.5%: H1 at 2.8% (2% excluding overlay); management says it is ahead of guidance.
Standalone ROA FY27 guidance of 3.5-4%: H1 reported 4.3%, above the top of the range even after the INR50 crore overlay.
Consolidated AUM growth FY27 guidance of 20-25%: H1 growth 9% (about 19% annualised); management expects to land in the range and aims for the upper band (25%+).
Long-term target of INR32,000 crore consolidated AUM by FY30 unchanged, with about 30% from non-MFI; company says it has achieved about 50% of the target.
Stable NIM of about 14.5% expected on a cross-cycle basis; management will pass through cost-of-funds changes to lending rates.
Overlay target: around INR100 crore total buffer, with management saying it may stop there if not needed.
Branch openings: about 50 in H2 FY27 and 100-150 in FY28.
capex_capacity: Branches: 2,075 total across 27 states and 5 union territories; 19 SFL branches added in Q2.
Planned branch openings of about 50 in H2 FY27 and 100-150 in FY28.
Liquidity of about INR2,235 crore as of 30 September; undrawn sanctions of about INR4,600 crore (management also cited 'more than INR4,000 crore' and INR2,200 crore liquidity on the call).
Raised about INR2,630 crore in Q2 and INR5,630 crore in H1 FY27.
Promoter warrants of INR100 crore at INR260 per share (17% above SEBI formula price of INR222); first tranche of INR25 crore received.
demand_pricing: Client base 34.1 lakh across 2,075 branches; 1.9 lakh new clients in Q2 and 4.2 lakh in H1 FY27.
Sourcing-to-disbursement ratio 34%; disbursement-area ratio (DA) in the 21-23% band.
Karnataka and Maharashtra are each about 1% of on-book portfolio; no repayment stress seen in those states.
Assam floods: 42,394 borrowers moratorium, about 90% resumed repayment during the moratorium; the company will pass the full NATCAT insurance payout to affected customers.
Ex-bucket collection efficiency 99.8%; PAR 1 at 2.9% (2.92%), down from 5.79% a year ago; October collections said to be practically the same as September.
Cashless collections reached 25% of total; disbursements 100% cashless. Average instalment below INR2,000, so management sees minimal UPI MDR impact.
Write-offs in Q2 about INR72-73 crore; recoveries of INR16 crore against write-offs in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any micro-market or state-level stress, and are Karnataka and Maharashtra showing repayment issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no state shows stress; drought states are negligible exposure, and repayment in Karnataka and Maharashtra is not stressed. Collection efficiency is 99.5-99.8% across states, including Assam.

qa_highlights.question: What is the policy on the management overlay given PCR of 133%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants a buffer that can insulate against microfinance cycles. The overlay was INR50 crore (INR36 crore plus INR14 crore added this quarter), with an internal target of about INR100 crore, after which it may stop.

qa_highlights.question: Could guidance be raised given 31% YoY AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditi Singh said the 31% includes strong Q3 and Q4 of last year; sequential H1 growth of 9% annualises to about 19%. Management expects to reach the upper band (25%+) of the 20-25% range; no ROA guidance revision was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the overlay in the ECL model show a 1.2% gap between reported and adjusted credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditi Singh explained ECL is re-run from scratch each quarter, so the full INR50 crore is treated as overlay and the earlier INR36 crore was also not required by the model.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the NIM rise to 15.9% and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher yield from better portfolio quality, lower cost of funds and higher DA contributed. Management sees a stable cross-cycle NIM of about 14.5%-15%, with quarterly aberrations possible.

qa_highlights.question: How will floating-rate borrowings reprice if rates rise?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of borrowings are floating, repricing on six-month or annual cycles per sanction terms; management negotiates upward moves with lenders and says it would pass cost increases to customers to protect the 14.5% NIM.

qa_highlights.question: Is the non-MFI housing segment recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: Satin Housing is re-engineering its product from urban affordable to rural housing; growth is expected to start in about two quarters, but it will not be as strong as SFL.

qa_highlights.question: Are the DA income and FX/derecognition gains one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no one-off incomes; DA is in a steady 21-23% band, and the income is recurring, though the servicing cost of earlier assignments offsets it over time.

risks_watch: Sustainability of the 14.5% cross-cycle NIM given Q2 NIM of 15.9% and possible policy-rate hikes; about 50% of borrowings are floating, repricing on six-month or annual cycles per sanction terms.
Whether consolidated AUM growth reaches the 20-25% FY27 guidance: H1 growth was 9% (about 19% annualised), so H2 disbursements must carry the year.
Management overlay path: total buffer of about INR50 crore against an internal target of about INR100 crore; reported ROA and credit cost depend on further top-ups.
Satin Housing Finance recovery after two quarters of slowed origination and the shift from urban affordable to rural housing; growth expected to lag SFL.
Stress from the drought states (Karnataka, Maharashtra) and upcoming state elections, which management says are negligible in exposure but were not quantified beyond a 1% share each.
Consolidated returns still carry subsidiary fixed costs (SFL, housing, QTrino, Satin Growth Alternatives); operating leverage yet to show, and UPI MDR impact to be watched on loan repayments.
key_quotes: So the entire INR50 crores is an overlay.
We have therefore absorbed roughly 100 plus basis points of ROA into the balance sheet, and we had every opportunity to declare more stellar profits.
We are approaching the range rather than inside it and we want to be straightforward about that.
There is no one-off income which is there which is reflected in the profit.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, provisioning and the decision to hold back reported profit through the overlay, and firm that FY27 guidance on credit cost and ROA is being beaten. More cautious and less specific on AUM growth, admitting H1 is below the 20-25% range, and on NIM sustainability and floating-rate repricing, where answers were qualitative and sometimes repeated.

adds.what: About 50 new branches in H2 FY27

growth.why: Management holds FY27 consolidated AUM growth guidance of 20-25% (aiming for upper band) after 9% H1 growth (~19% annualised), backed by about 50 branch openings in H2 FY27 and 100-150 in FY28, disbursements up 48% in H1, and Q2 PPOP up 53% YoY; no capex figures or detailed order-book numbers were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 NIM rose to 15.9% from 14.3% last quarter, but management guides a stable cross-cycle NIM of about 14.5% and says quarterly aberrations are possible, so further expansion looks unlikely to be sustained; ROA is above guidance at 4.3% H1 reported.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 50 branch openings are planned in H2 FY27 and 100-150 in FY28 against a base of 2,075 branches, with 19 SFL branches already added in Q2.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 consolidated AUM growth was only 9% (about 19% annualised) but management still targets the upper band of 20-25% FY27 guidance, backed by H1 disbursements up 48% YoY and Q2 disbursements of INR3,697 crore (+41%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex figures were given and the branch model is asset-light, but the INR32,000 crore FY30 AUM target (about 50% achieved) and 100-150 FY28 branch openings imply continued investment without a stated new capex plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Credit cost H1 is 2.8% against 3-3.5% FY27 guidance and ROA H1 is 4.3% against 3.5-4%, so management says it is ahead, but AUM growth is below range and no guidance revision was announced.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Asset quality is improving with standalone GNPA at 1.9% (from 2.2% in June), PAR 1 at 2.9% (from 5.79% a year ago) and collection efficiency of 99.8%, so credit cost and ROA guidance look safe, though AUM growth carries risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Satin Housing is re-engineering toward rural housing with growth expected in about two quarters, and QTrino is progressing toward quantum-safe cybersecurity certification, but no firm launch dates were given.

rows.label: Undrawn sanctions support AUM growth
rows.why: Undrawn sanctions of about INR4,600 crore (management also cited more than INR4,000 crore) and liquidity of about INR2,235 crore give funding for H2 disbursements needed to reach 20-25% AUM growth.

rows.label: Overlay top-ups absorb reported profit
rows.why: Overlay is INR50 crore against an internal target of about INR100 crore, which equals about 100 bps of ROA; further top-ups would hold reported ROA down, although management says it may stop at target.

rows.label: Leverage falls as capital is raised
rows.why: Leverage fell to 2.9x from 3.2x and CRAR rose to 27.89% after raising INR2,630 crore in Q2 and INR5,630 crore in H1 FY27, leaving room for growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality, provisioning, and beating FY27 credit cost and ROA guidance, but cautious and vague on AUM growth below range, NIM sustainability and floating-rate repricing, while analysts pressed on the overlay policy, the 9% H1 AUM growth and the DA and FX income qualit
